fills.researcher_notes: Applying the core brief's standing GTSOU determination to this corridor (this is the 'answer once per company' question, and this is the only row in this brief with the Operator flag). tsoua.com is 403 live (WAF, per protocol gotcha 1); read via its Wayback capture instead. That capture's site footer gives the exact legal name GEM should carry: 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, Limited Liability Company' (info@tsoua.com, Kyiv). I'm proposing the shorter form already used in this row's own Owner cell ('Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine [100.%]') for naming consistency within the row, rather than the sheet carrying two different renderings of the same entity. Crucially the same capture is not just a general GTSOU-is-the-national-TSO source — it's GTSOU's own news item about 'the accident at the KZU-1 gas pipeline section in Kyiv region' (dateline 17 Sep 2020), i.e. it names GTSOU as the operator of THIS specific system (KЗУ = «Kyїv – Zakhidnyi kordon», the corridor P0777/P1480 both describe), not merely of the Ukrainian GTS in general, closing the 'name the entity operating THIS section' bar in the protocol. Independent corroboration: uk.wikipedia.org's Газотранспортна система України article cites the 30 Dec 2019 transit agreement among Naftogaz, 'ТОВ «Оператор ГТС України»' and Gazprom, i.e. an independent (non-GTSOU) source giving the same Ukrainian legal name and confirming the 2020 handover date. Does not extend to occupied-territory or Russian-side rows (out of scope for this brief). [Leg-3 review 2026-08-15] Independence check: the original pair was a GTSOU news item plus a Ukrainian-language Wikipedia article; a tertiary encyclopaedia is not a second independent ORIGIN. Added ENTSOG's member list (third-party European TSO association) so the high tier rests on operator-primary + third-party, with the Wikipedia link retained as a reading aid and NOT counted toward independence.

validity.recommendation: Do not change LengthKnownKm on the strength of the measured 503 km schematic draw alone (ratio 0.45) — per protocol gotcha 3 a shorter-than-stated schematic draw is the commonest, non-diagnostic shape here, and P0777 is not one of the two named exceeding-length exceptions (P0784, P1481). But separately: I obtained the Ukrtransgaz historical-development chronology via Wayback (utg.ua 403s live per gotcha 1; this is the exact document the source_ladder names as 'the one thing that would close cluster A', previously unreachable). It documents the dedicated «Kyїv – Zakhidnyi kordon Ukrayiny» build in four discrete entries: 1970 (I nitka/string) 183.6 km ∅1020mm; 1972 (II nitka/string) 216.3 km ∅1220mm; a 1973 'II cherha' (second construction stage, undocumented length) built alongside the Shebelynka–Dykanka–Kyiv line; and a further 1974 entry of 42.8 km ∅1200mm. None of these, singly or summed (183.6+216.3+42.8=442.7 km, plus whatever the undated 1973 stage adds), reaches anywhere near P0777's stated 1112.00 km. The chronology also states the 1970 «Kyїv–Zakhidnyi kordon» build was explicitly the 'first stage of the continuation' of the separate, longer Yefremivka–Dykanka–Kyiv trunk — i.e. the KЗУ-branded corridor is documented as sitting downstream of a much longer eastern trunk. That raises a real possibility that 1112.00 conflates the dedicated KЗУ system with all or part of that upstream trunk (the aggregate/whole-corridor-on-one-row pattern already flagged as motif #2 in the protocol), rather than 1112 being simply wrong. I could not find a documented figure matching 1112 km anywhere in this source, so I'm flagging this as a genuine open question rather than asserting a verdict — a human should reconcile it against the staged cluster A finding (367+506=873 km), which used different source material than this chronology and predates my access to it.
validity.researcher_notes: Searched: Ukrtransgaz historical chronology (utg.ua, via Wayback, see proposed_refs) — four KZU-specific construction entries found, none summing to 1112 km; explicit statement that the KZU corridor continues the separate Yefremivka–Dykanka–Kyiv trunk. Searched the same document for a Shebelynka–Dykanka–Kyiv or Yefremivka–Dykanka–Kyiv length figure that might explain 1112 as a combined-corridor total; none given. Did not find an independent second source with a length figure for P0777's specific scope (Kyiv–Uzhhorod), so this stays a concern, not a fill.
